title: Worst affine-class representative under two-round MELP
summary: Decide whether an involutional S-box is always the worst representative of its affine-equivalence class for two-round linear potential.

formal_statement.body: For every involutional S-box $S$, every affine-equivalent representative $S^{\prime}$, and every admissible $\mathbb F_{2^m}$-linear MDS layer $M$, is $\operatorname{MELP}_2(S,M)\geq\operatorname{MELP}_2(S^{\prime},M)$? Prove the universal ordering or give a concrete triple $(S,S^{\prime},M)$ that reverses it.

scope.domain: Affine-equivalent S-box representatives in two-round AES-like SPNs under linear cryptanalysis.
assumptions: $M$ is an admissible field-linear MDS layer.
scope.unresolved_remainder: No proof of the universal MELP ordering and no reversing affine-equivalent counterexample was found.

progress.summary: The source asks whether involutional S-boxes are universally worst within their affine-equivalence classes under two-round MELP.
